title: SOMEONE INSIDE
excerpt: Maya discovers that someone has been living inside her apartment's hidden maintenance space.
content:
The message arrived at 11:43 p.m.

Maya Cole stared at the screen until the letters began to blur.

**TOMORROW AT MIDNIGHT, ONE OF THEM WILL DIE. CHOOSE CAREFULLY.**

Below it was another line.

**YOU HAVE ALREADY MADE THIS CHOICE ONCE.**

She lowered the phone.

Across the room, Rebecca Okafor sat on the edge of the bed, her hands clasped tightly between her knees. Evelyn stood beside the window, watching the dark street below.

Neither woman looked surprised.

That frightened Maya more than the message.

“Who sent it?” she asked.

Rebecca gave a tired laugh. “You still think this is about a message?”

“Then explain it.”

“I can't.”

“Can't or won't?”

Rebecca looked at her. “You want the truth? Fine. The truth is that every time somebody tells you what happened at Meridian House, you remember something different. Every time you get close to the truth, someone dies. And every time you think you're making your own decision, you're following instructions someone planted in your head years ago.”

Maya felt her stomach tighten.

Evelyn turned from the window.

“Rebecca, that's enough.”

“No,” Rebecca snapped. “She deserves to know.”

“Then tell her everything,” Evelyn said quietly. “Tell her what happened to Subject 014.”

The room went silent.

Maya looked between them.

“Stop calling me that.”

Rebecca stood.

“Subject 014 wasn't just a patient, Maya. You were the first successful experiment.”

“Experiment in what?”

“Memory.”

Maya shook her head. “I know what happened to my memories. My father died. My mother—”

“Your father didn't die the way you remember.”

The words landed like a physical blow.

Maya stepped backwards.

“Don't.”

“Samuel Cole was part of Project Lazarus. He helped build the original memory archive. When he discovered what they were doing, he tried to destroy it.”

“My father was an engineer.”

“He was much more than that.”

Evelyn moved toward Maya, but Maya raised a hand.

“Don't touch me.”

Rebecca continued.

“Your father discovered that Meridian House wasn't simply erasing memories. They were transferring them, storing them, and using them to create people who could remember things they had never experienced.”

Maya stared at her.

“That's impossible.”

“That's what I said.”

Rebecca reached into her jacket and removed a small photograph.

It showed a young girl standing in front of a white building. Beside her was a man with one hand resting on her shoulder.

Maya recognised the girl immediately.

It was her.

The man was Samuel Cole.

But the photograph was dated three years after the date her father supposedly died.

Maya took it.

Her fingers trembled.

“Where did you get this?”

“Room 7.”

“Who took it?”

“Your father.”

Maya looked at the back of the photograph.

There were six handwritten words.

**SHE MUST NEVER REMEMBER WHAT I DID.**

For a moment, the room seemed to tilt.

“What did he do?”

Rebecca didn't answer.

Evelyn did.

“He saved your life.”

***

At 12:16 a.m., someone knocked on the apartment door.

Three slow knocks.

Maya froze.

Rebecca reached beneath her jacket and pulled out a small pistol.

Evelyn whispered, “Nobody should know we're here.”

The knocking came again.

Three times.

Then a voice.

“Maya?”

Daniel Okafor.

Maya felt a wave of anger so intense that it almost drowned out her fear.

She moved toward the door.

Rebecca caught her wrist.

“Don't.”

“It's my editor.”

“That's exactly why you shouldn't open it.”

Daniel knocked again.

“Maya, I know you're in there. Please. It's important.”

Maya looked through the peephole.

Daniel stood alone in the corridor, his shirt untucked and his face covered in sweat.

He looked terrified.

She opened the door but kept the chain fastened.

“What are you doing here?”

Daniel glanced over his shoulder.

“Let me in.”

“Answer me first.”

“Someone followed me.”

“Who?”

“I don't know.”

Maya studied his face.

“Did you know about Meridian House?”

Daniel looked down.

That was enough.

She shut the door.

“Maya, wait!”

“You knew.”

“I can explain.”

“You knew about Project Lazarus.”

“I knew parts of it.”

“You knew Rebecca was alive?”

Daniel's face changed.

Behind Maya, Rebecca stepped into view.

Daniel stared at her as if he had seen a ghost.

“Rebecca?”

She raised the pistol.

“Don't say my name.”

Daniel's eyes filled with tears.

“God. You're alive.”

“That's what you told everyone I wasn't.”

“I thought you were dead.”

“You signed the report.”

Daniel looked at Maya.

“Please. You have to understand. They threatened my family.”

Rebecca laughed bitterly.

“Your family? You mean the family you left behind while you helped them bury me?”

Daniel had no answer.

Maya removed the door chain.

“Get inside.”

Rebecca turned sharply.

“Maya!”

“If he knows something, I want to hear it.”

Daniel entered slowly.

The moment the door closed, he placed both hands on the dining table.

“Meridian House has been watching you for years,” he said. “Not because you're a journalist. Because of what your father left inside you.”

Maya folded her arms.

“What's inside me?”

“The original archive key.”

Rebecca lowered the pistol slightly.

“No.”

Daniel nodded.

“Your father didn't destroy the archive. He transferred the access sequence into your memory.”

Maya stared at him.

“How?”

“That's what Project Lazarus was designed to do. The human brain became the safest storage device they could find.”

“That makes no sense.”

“It doesn't have to make sense. It only has to work.”

Daniel reached into his pocket and placed a small black device on the table.

It was about the size of a flash drive.

“Your father gave me this before he disappeared.”

Maya looked at it.

“You said he died.”

“I was told he died.”

“You were my editor. You had access to every story I wrote. You knew where I lived. You knew everything about me.”

Daniel lowered his head.

“I was assigned to watch you.”

The words seemed to suck all the air from the room.

“For how long?”

“Eleven years.”

Maya slapped him.

The sound cracked through the apartment.

Daniel didn't move.

“Eleven years,” she repeated. “You sat across from me every morning. You read my work. You asked about my mother. You attended my father's memorial.”

“I know.”

“You let me believe I was losing my mind.”

“I was trying to keep you alive.”

“By lying to me?”

Daniel looked up.

“By keeping you away from the archive.”

Rebecca stepped closer.

“Then why are you here now?”

Daniel looked at her.

“Because the people who run Meridian House have decided Maya is no longer useful.”

“Who?”

He hesitated.

Then he said a name.

“Dr. Shaw.”

***

At 2:08 a.m., Maya opened her laptop.

Daniel had connected the black device to it. A folder appeared on the screen.

PROJECT LAZARUS — ORIGINAL ARCHIVE.

Inside were hundreds of files.

Most were labelled with numbers.

001.

002.

003.

014.

015.

Maya clicked on her own number.

A video opened.

The recording was grainy, but the room was unmistakable. White walls. A metal chair. A camera mounted in the ceiling.

Maya recognised the room from her nightmares.

A younger version of herself sat in the chair.

She couldn't have been more than seventeen.

A man stood behind the camera.

Dr. Shaw.

“Subject 014,” he said. “Do you know why you're here?”

The girl shook her head.

“Do you remember your father?”

“Yes.”

“What happened to him?”

“He died.”

“How?”

The girl looked down.

“He died in a car accident.”

Shaw smiled.

“Good. And what did he tell you before he died?”

The girl began to cry.

“He said I shouldn't trust you.”

The video paused.

Maya stared at the screen.

“Play it.”

Daniel pressed the space bar.

Shaw moved closer to the girl.

“Your father was a dangerous man, Maya. He wanted to hurt you.”

“No.”

“He put something inside your head.”

“No!”

“Do you know what it is?”

The girl shook her head.

Shaw leaned closer.

“Then let's find out.”

The recording ended.

Maya pushed away from the laptop.

Her hands were shaking.

“I remember that room.”

Rebecca moved beside her.

“It's coming back.”

Maya closed her eyes.

A flash.

A bright light.

A needle.

Her father's voice.

Then a door slamming.

She opened her eyes.

“There's another file.”

Daniel looked at the screen.

“Which one?”

“015.”

Rebecca went still.

Maya clicked it.

A video appeared.

Rebecca was sitting in the same chair.

Her hair was shorter. Her face was bruised.

Shaw stood behind her.

“Subject 015. State your name.”

“Rebecca Okafor.”

“Who is Daniel Okafor?”

“My brother.”

“Does he know what happened here?”

“No.”

“Would he help you escape?”

Rebecca looked directly into the camera.

“Yes.”

Shaw sighed.

“Then we may have a problem.”

The recording continued.

A second voice came from somewhere outside the frame.

“Doctor, we have a visitor.”

Shaw turned.

“Who?”

The answer came clearly.

“Samuel Cole.”

Maya stopped breathing.

The camera shook.

A man entered the room.

Her father.

Alive.

He looked older, thinner, but unmistakably Samuel Cole.

He walked directly toward Rebecca.

“I'm sorry,” he said.

Rebecca began to cry.

Then Samuel turned toward the camera.

His eyes seemed to look directly at Maya.

“If you're watching this,” he said, “then I've failed.”

The screen went black.

***

At 4:31 a.m., Maya stood alone on the balcony.

Lagos was beginning to wake beneath her. The first buses moved through the streets. A generator rattled somewhere nearby. A woman shouted at a neighbour across the compound.

Ordinary sounds.

An ordinary morning.

But Maya's life had become something else.

She had spent years believing her father was dead.

Now she had seen him alive in a room where people were being experimented on.

Her phone vibrated.

Unknown number.

**YOU FOUND THE ARCHIVE.**

Another message appeared.

**NOW FIND THE PERSON WHO OPENED THE DOOR.**

Maya looked back into the apartment.

Daniel was asleep on the sofa.

Rebecca sat at the table, watching the laptop.

Evelyn was in the kitchen.

Three people.

Three possible suspects.

She typed:

**WHO OPENED THE DOOR?**

The reply came almost immediately.

**THE PERSON YOU TRUST MOST.**

Maya turned.

“Rebecca?”

Rebecca looked up.

“What?”

“Did you know my father was alive?”

Rebecca didn't answer quickly enough.

Maya stepped inside.

“Did you know?”

Rebecca stood.

“I saw him that night.”

“And you never told me?”

“He made me promise.”

“Why?”

“Because he said the people watching you would kill you if you remembered.”

Maya shook her head.

“You all keep saying you were protecting me.”

Rebecca's voice broke.

“Because we were.”

“Then why does everyone around me know more about my life than I do?”

Before Rebecca could answer, Daniel woke up.

“What's happening?”

Maya ignored him.

She looked at Rebecca.

“Who opened the door at Meridian House?”

Rebecca's face went pale.

“I don't know.”

A sound came from the laptop.

A notification.

A new file had appeared inside the archive.

No number.

No title.

Just a date.

**TODAY.**

Maya clicked it.

A live video opened.

The camera showed the apartment.

Their apartment.

The angle was from somewhere near the ceiling.

Maya could see herself standing beside Rebecca.

She could see Daniel on the sofa.

She could see Evelyn in the kitchen.

Then a figure entered the frame behind Evelyn.

A man.

He wore a dark shirt and black gloves.

Maya spun around.

The kitchen was empty.

She looked back at the screen.

The man was still there.

Standing directly behind Evelyn.

Then he lifted his head.

His face came into view.

Maya recognised him.

It was Dr. Shaw.

The video ended.

A message appeared.

**YOU HAVE ONE DAY LEFT.**

Then another.

**AND YOU STILL HAVEN'T ASKED YOUR MOTHER WHAT SHE DID.**

Maya slowly turned toward the kitchen.

Evelyn stood in the doorway.

Her expression had changed.

For the first time since Maya had seen her again, she looked afraid.

“Mum,” Maya whispered.

Evelyn closed her eyes.

“I can explain.”

Maya took one step toward her.

“What did you do?”

Evelyn looked at Rebecca.

Then at Daniel.

Finally, she looked at her daughter.

“I was the one who gave them your name.”

Silence.

Maya felt something inside her collapse.

“You sent me to Meridian House?”

Evelyn began to cry.

“I thought they were going to help you.”

“Help me with what?”

Evelyn's lips trembled.

“With the memories of the night you killed your father.”

Maya stumbled backwards.

“No.”

Evelyn reached for her.

“Maya—”

“No!”

The laptop chimed again.

A final file opened automatically.

The title read:

**SUBJECT 014 — FINAL MEMORY RESTORATION.**

Maya stared at the screen.

A countdown appeared.

23:59:59.

23:59:58.

23:59:57.

And beneath it, a sentence:

**REMEMBER WHAT YOU DID BEFORE MIDNIGHT.**

END OF EPISODE 4

### NEXT: EPISODE 5 — THE NIGHT SHE FORGOT
